For polynomial test functions, we establish a finite limit for the normalized variance and prove a central limit theorem under suitable connection-profile integrability and vertex mark moment assumptions. When the limiting variance is positive, the normalized statistics admit an $O(|W_n|^{-1/2})$ normal-approximation bound in both Wasserstein and Kolmogorov distance. Furthermore, under an exponential moment assumption on the vertex marks, we extend the central limit theorem to a general class of test functions $f$.

papers.title: Power projections, Gram structures, and finite-field lifting of Butson Hadamard matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper we investigate the algebraic properties of Hadamard powers of Butson Hadamard matrices $H\in \mathrm{BH}(n,3p)$, and show that for certain parameter values the cube root projection matrix $H^{\circ p}$ has the same structure as the adjacency matrix of a strongly regular graph. Then, by using a simple eigenvalue analysis we show, among other results, the nonexistence of $\mathrm{BH}(17,15)$ matrices. For other parameter values, a more in-depth study and in particular, a complete classification of all possible projection matrices is necessary. We carry out this task for the case of $\mathrm{BH}(16,15)$ matrices, and using finite field techniques we show that none of these projections can be lifted up to form a Butson matrix. In particular, we show the nonexistence of $\mathrm{BH}(16,15)$ matrices for the first time.

papers.title: Counting $6$-Cliques in $O(n^{5.97})$ time and $O(\log n)$ space
papers.abstract: We present an algorithm that, given read-only access to the adjacency matrix of an $n$-vertex graph $G$, computes the number of $6$-cliques in $G$ using $O(n^{5.97})$ time and $O(\log n)$ space. We achieve this by exploiting a decomposition of an equality indicator function underlying, among others, the refutations of the Exponential Time Hypothesis by OpenAI and Anthropic, and of the $k$-Clique Conjecture by Vassilevska Williams and Zamir [arXiv, 2026]. Via known reductions, this implies an $O(1.994^n)$ time and polynomial space algorithm for Max Cut on $n$-vertex graphs.

papers.title: Infinity-Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Principal Component Analysis: Exact Reformulation, Finite-Sample Guarantee, and Efficient Algorithm
papers.abstract: Principal component analysis (PCA) is a fundamental and ubiquitous technique for dimension reduction and representation learning, yet its empirical formulation remains vulnerable to distributional uncertainty. While distributionally robust optimization (DRO) offers a natural remedy, existing order-2 Wasserstein models of PCA either preserve the nominal PCA subspace or lack an exact reformulation. This paper demonstrates how the infinity-Wasserstein distance can reconcile these two desirable properties. For the resulting DRO model of PCA, we derive an exact finite-dimensional reformulation and explicitly identify a worst-case distribution attaining the inner maximum. Crucially, the reformulated objective retains samplewise residual information beyond the empirical covariance matrix, revealing a mechanism through which distributional robustness can reshape the learned principal subspace. Under the mild assumption that the true distribution has a finite fourth moment, we further establish a uniform finite-sample performance guarantee for the proposed model. An iteratively reweighted majorization-minimization algorithm is also developed to solve the resulting nonconvex and nonsmooth optimization problem, with a rigorous analysis of its convergence properties. Numerical experiments substantiate the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithm and the practical effectiveness of the infinity-Wasserstein model in downstream applications.

papers.title: Berry Esseen bounds for fractional Vasicek type processes: continuous and high-frequency regimes
papers.abstract: We study the estimation of the drift parameters $(a,b)$ of the fractional Vasicek process $dX_t=a(b-X_t)\,dt+dB^H_t$, driven by a fractional Brownian motion of Hurst index $H\in(0,1)$. The estimators are of moment type, built from the empirical mean and variance of the path, and are analysed in two regimes: continuous observation on $[0,T]$, and high-frequency observation at times $t_i=iΔ_n$ with $Δ_n\to0$ and $T_n=nΔ_n\to\infty$. Using the Malliavin--Stein method on the second Wiener chaos, we prove consistency of both estimators for every $H$, and quantitative central limit theorems in the Wasserstein distance: for $H<\frac34$ for the estimator of $a$, with explicit rates depending on $H$, and for every $H\in(0,1)$ for the estimator of $b$, at the rate $T^{-H}$. In the discrete regime the bounds contain an additional discretization term of order $Δ_n^{\min\{H+1/2,\,1\}}$, and for $H<\frac12$ the central limit theorem for the estimator of $b$ requires in addition $T_n^{1-2H}Δ_n^{1+2H}\to0$. A short Monte Carlo study illustrates the results.

papers.title: Kernel Regression using Persistence Diagrams
papers.abstract: Persistence diagrams are widely used in topological data analysis to summarize topological and geometric structure in data. We study nonparametric regression where inputs are persistence diagrams and outputs are real-valued. Using kernel-based local averaging estimators defined directly over diagram space with Wasserstein distance, we establish consistency and derive bounds on the rate of convergence under suitable assumptions in the $L^2$-theory. We also present computational experiments that demonstrate strong performance of the proposed estimator, particularly in low data regimes.

papers.title: A comparative exploration of Steinerberger curvature and resistance curvature in model and real-world complex networks
papers.abstract: Discrete curvature extends the concept of curvature from continuous spaces to discrete structures such as graphs and networks. It provides a mathematical framework for characterising local and global network geometry, that offers insights into structural properties such as connectivity and clustering. In this study, we investigate Steinerberger curvature (SBC) and resistance curvature (RC) and examine their relationships with established graph curvature measures, namely Forman-Ricci, Augmented Forman-Ricci, and Ollivier-Ricci curvatures, a notion of scalar sectional curvature, as well as conventional vertex-based measures. A systematic comparative analysis is conducted across various synthetic network models and real-world networks, focusing on curvature distributions, correlations with structural measures, and the identification of structurally important vertices through network disintegration experiments based on global efficiency. Our results show that SBC generally exhibits weaker correlations with other measures. On the other hand, RC is strongly positively correlated with established discrete Ricci curvature measures, whereas it is predominantly negatively correlated with conventional vertex-based measures like degree and centrality-based measures. Furthermore, RC achieves a reduction in communication efficiency comparable to or faster than established Ricci curvature measures. These findings suggest that SBC captures structural characteristics that are largely distinct from those reflected by other measures, while RC exhibits distinct structural associations and shows significant potential for identifying vertices critical to network connectivity.

papers.title: Quantum Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport in spacetime through spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac distributions and spatiotemporal states
papers.abstract: Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport is a mathematical framework that determines the most efficient way to transform one probability distribution into another while minimizing a given cost function. Its central constructions include the Wasserstein distances, which quantify the space of probability distributions, and dual formulations that link to convex analysis. Its standard quantum generalization replaces probability distributions with density operators and cost function with positive semidefinite cost operator, which should be regarded as spatial quantum optimal transport. In this work, we propose the quantum optimal transport problem in spacetime through the spatiotemporal phase-space Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distribution and spatiotemporal states and through spatiotemporal state. We show that the two formalisms are equivalent and related via spatiotemporal operator frames. In the Kirkwood-Dirac phase-space formalism, the spatiotemporal distribution and the cost function are complex-valued, and the spatiotemporal couplings are Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distributions that yield the correct marginals for the local states. In the spatiotemporal state formalism, the cost operators are generally non-Hermitian, and the spatiotemporal couplings are generally non-Hermitian and yield the correct reduced local states. The Margenau-Hill phase-space distribution gives rise to a real-valued optimal transport in spatiotemporal phase space; in the spatiotemporal state formalism, this corresponds to a Hermitian spatiotemporal coupling state. We give a rigorous definitions and a careful discussion of its duality. We also introduce a spatiotemporal quantum Wasserstein metric based on a metric in spatiotemporal phase spaces and show that it satisfies the metric axioms.

papers.title: Spectral Stability and Convergence of the Unnormalized Graph Laplacian on Noisy Point Clouds
papers.abstract: The first eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the unnormalized graph Laplacian of clean samples from a manifold, suitably scaled, approximate those of a weighted Laplace-Beltrami operator. However, the samples are usually observed with noise and therefore need not lie on the manifold. We build the clean and noisy graph Laplacians, with bandwidth $\varepsilon$, on the clean samples and on the noisy observations, where the noise is arbitrary but bounded by $δ$. We show that, with high probability, the first eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the noisy graph Laplacian are close to those of the clean one: the eigenvalues within $O(δ/\varepsilon)$, and the subspaces spanned by the first eigenvectors within $O(\sqrt{δ/\varepsilon})$, whether or not the eigenvalues are simple. Consequently, if $δ$ is small enough relative to $\varepsilon$, the noisy graph Laplacian approximates the weighted Laplace-Beltrami operator at the same rate as the clean one. We also show that, for large noise, we can get the same rate as the clean graph Laplacian by first using a denoiser, and then building the graph Laplacian on the denoised observations.

papers.title: Approximating Itô Processes in Adapted Wasserstein Distance with Finite Support Laws
papers.abstract: Motivated by finite-scenario surrogates in stopping and control problems, we study the approximation of Itô diffusion laws by laws supported on $M$ paths in an adapted Wasserstein distance, which we term adapted functional quantization. Under the strict adapted Wasserstein distance, no finite-support approximation can achieve vanishing error, while even under its relaxed counterpart, naive empirical measures still fail to converge. To resolve this, we develop a recursive conditional sampling algorithm and derive constructive upper bounds on the adapted quantization error. In one dimension, this yields the Brownian rate $(\log M)^{-1/2}$ for every diffusion with continuous coefficients of linear growth and pathwise uniqueness. In several dimensions, a quantitative Osgood stability condition with exponent $β$ yields the rate $(\log M)^{-η_p}$, where $η_p=\min\{1/2,β/(β+4p-2)\}$. Without the Osgood condition, we construct a two-dimensional diffusion with smooth bounded coefficients whose adapted quantization error decays more slowly than $(\log M)^{-γ}$ for any $γ>0$.

papers.title: Asymptotic enumeration of histories and limit laws in two random graph evolution models
papers.abstract: We study growth models for random graphs where the growth is established by vertex or edge creations and where there is no dependence between vertices and edges. Creations are logged by time stamps such that the history of the resulting graph can be reconstructed. We investigate two prototypical models, an undirected and a directed one, called undirected independent growth model (UIG-model) and directed independent growth model (DIG-model). The generating functions for the number of histories have radius of convergence equal to zero. In the UIG-model, we express the asymptotic number of histories as a sum that is amenable to the discrete Laplace method. We derive the asymptotic number of histories, study the number of vertices of a random history, and prove a central limit theorem. In the DIG-model we use a rescaled Borel transform to get an entire function. Then we show that this function is Hayman admissible, which enables us to derive the asymptotic number of histories in this model. The counting sequence is closely related to the framework of generalized Legendre-Stirling numbers. To determine the number of vertices in a random history, we prove that the bivariate generating function is e-admissible and infer that again a normal limit law holds. Finally, we discuss a correspondence to set partitions with even block sizes and present an algorithm based on Boltzmann samplers that generates such graphs uniformly at random.

papers.title: Cutoff on abelian groups
papers.abstract: We prove the long-predicted equivalence between the cutoff phenomenon and the product condition along any sequence of abelian random walks whose inverse transition probabilities grow at most logarithmically with the size of the group. Our result does not require reversibility, and comes with a sharp quantitative estimate on the mixing window. Moreover, we show that our sparsity restriction is optimal by constructing abelian Cayley graphs which satisfy the product condition but fail to exhibit cutoff, and whose degrees are arbitrarily close to being logarithmic in the volume.

papers.title: Wasserstein Target Diagram for Model Evaluation
papers.abstract: The target diagram is often used in geosciences, which provides a visualization tool for model evaluation and shows the temporal or spatial matching of data. However, its construction requires paired data of equal sample sizes, limiting its application to model comparisons involving unpaired samples or probability distributions. In this study, we propose the Wasserstein target diagram based on the 2-Wasserstein distance from optimal transport. Unlike the original target diagram, the Wasserstein target diagram does not require paired data of equal sizes and evaluates models from the probability distribution perspective. We further establish that the two target diagrams coincide when the given paired data are comonotone, which is common in climate science, such as cumulative precipitation and solar radiation. Through two simulation studies and an application to wind speed distribution fitting, we demonstrate that the proposed diagram can detect the probability distribution discrepancies that the original target diagram may not distinguish. The Wasserstein target diagram therefore lifts the model evaluation to the probability level and provides a complementary approach to estimating the agreement in probability distributions.

papers.title: Size-Independent Survival Bounds for Routing Without a Map
papers.abstract: A walker, such as a packet carrying a secret share, must reach a known target in an unknown graph while avoiding a fixed set of fatal vertices (compromised relays in the packet interpretation). It learns a vertex's neighbours only on reaching that vertex safely, remembers its observations, and is promised a safe route. We prove that a randomised depth-first strategy guarantees a success probability depending only on the maximum degree and the number of fatal vertices, not on the size of the graph. Planarity is not required for this guarantee, and planar examples attain the bound at every sufficiently large graph size. At those sizes, when the degree cap is at least three, the guarantee is optimal among strict depth-first strategies. Whether strategies allowed to switch between unfinished branches can guarantee a larger worst-case survival probability remains open. For unknown trees and for graphs of maximum degree two, we determine the exact best worst-case success probability over all routing strategies. Explicit examples compare our strategy with random-priority frontier routing and ordinary random walks, showing how exploration order can prevent survival probability from declining as the graph grows.

papers.title: DLS: Dual-Logic Graph Neural Networks with Chaos-Fuzzy Residuals for Robust Link Prediction
papers.abstract: Link prediction is a fundamental task in graph mining, critical for applications ranging from biological interaction discovery to recommender systems. While Message Passing Neural Networks (MPNNs) have achieved state-of-the-art results, they are fundamentally limited by the inadvertent suppression of high-frequency signals, as the recursive aggregation that stabilizes structural learning inherently leads to over-smoothing, rendering node representations indistinguishable in deep layers. This limitation is particularly severe in heterophilous graphs, where structural proximity does not imply feature similarity. In this paper, we propose DLS (Dual-Logic SAGE), a novel inductive framework designed to break the over-smoothing barrier via a "controlled instability" mechanism. Unlike conventional methods relying on static structural heuristics, DLS introduces a dynamic residual pipeline. First, a Chaotic Injection Module utilizes the Logistic Map to diversify the feature manifold, exploiting sensitivity to initial conditions to separate topologically similar but semantically distinct nodes. Second, to mitigate the aleatoric uncertainty introduced by chaotic dynamics, a Fuzzy-Logic Gating Mechanism applies soft-thresholding to filter noise and retain only high-confidence signals. Experimental results on diverse benchmarks demonstrate that DLS effectively balances feature discrimination with robustness, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art baselines in heterophilous settings while maintaining competitive efficiency on standard homophilous graphs.

papers.title: Maximum number of cells in a matroid subdivision of hypersimplex
papers.abstract: David Speyer proved that the maximum number of cells in a regular matroid subdivision of the hypersimplex $Δ(m,t)$ is $\binom{t-2}{m-1}$ , using the language of tropical geometry and properties of the Tutte polynomial of a matroid \cite[Theorem 6.1]{Speyer}. In this paper, we prove this result in general, i.e. for arbitrary matroid subdivisions including the non-regular ones. We perform a different combinatorial way using our results in \cite{HHH} and independent of tropical language.

papers.title: Matroid Connectedness and Component Decomposition: Breaking the Quadratic Barrier
papers.abstract: Deciding whether a matroid is connected and computing its connected components are two fundamental algorithmic problems in matroid theory. Since the 1970s, the best known algorithms for both problems have used $O(n^2)$ independence queries on an $n$-element ground set. Our main contribution is to break this quadratic barrier: we give a deterministic algorithm that computes all connected components of a matroid on $n$ elements with $O(n \log{n})$ independence queries. Our algorithm for component decomposition combines fundamental basis exchanges with a disjoint-set union data structure, avoiding the explicit construction of the fundamental graph. Moreover, we show that our algorithm is asymptotically optimal by giving a lower bound based on a simple information-theoretic argument: any (deterministic or bounded-error randomized) algorithm to compute connected components needs $Ω(n \log{n})$ independence queries. Then, we turn to the query complexity of deciding whether a matroid is connected. For this problem, we present an algorithm that uses $O(nh)$ independence queries, where $h \ge 1$ bounds the size of any chain of nonempty proper cyclic flats. The algorithm achieves asymptotically optimal linear query complexity on elementary split matroids, that include all paving matroids, and on arbitrary direct sums of uniform matroids.

papers.title: Mean Field Games: Large Sparse Network Limits and Laplexion Dynamics
papers.abstract: Dynamic games are considered with large subpopulations distributed over large sparse graphs, where each agent has mean field coupling with all agents within the same cluster and meanwhile receives impact from neighboring clusters. Tractable limit models are obtained via the network limits of graph Laplacian operators modelling second order interactions. The resulting mean field game (MFG) has what is called Laplexion dynamics. For ring and torus topology cases, solutions for linear quadratic Laplexion MFG systems with infinite populations on infinite node networks are obtained via a second order linear partial differential equation system. This work focusses on the relationship between the finite population model and the sparse network limit model. We prove an $ε$-Nash equilibrium property for the obtained decentralized strategies.

papers.title: Causal Input--Output Modeling with Prior Information
papers.abstract: We study the problem of inferring a causal input--output model from unpaired marginal observations and a given prior coupling. We formulate this problem using entropic causal optimal transport, which seeks a coupling that preserves the observed marginals, satisfies a one--sided causality constraint, and remains close to the prior. For Gaussian marginals and general quadratic costs, we prove that the optimal coupling is Gaussian and reduce the problem to a finite--dimensional optimization over covariance matrices. Using a Cholesky transformation to simplify the causality constraint, we derive a Lagrangian dual formulation and develop a block coordinate descent algorithm with explicit update formulas. We establish linear convergence of the algorithm, with explicit convergence rates, and prove stability of the optimal coupling under marginal covariance perturbations and derive a statistical error bound. We further show its equivalence to Sinkhorn iterations. Numerical experiments demonstrate the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithm and illustrate the predictive advantages of causal couplings.

papers.title: Critical heavy traffic and diffusion limits for shortest-of-d dynamic routing
papers.abstract: We study shortest-of-$d$ routing, with fixed $d\ge2$, in $N$ parallel queues with independent finite-state Markov service environments switching at rate $κ_N$. At the critical load $ρ_N=1-1/N$, the empirical measure of the centered queue lengths, under stationarity, converges in distribution to a random probability measure determined by its mean. We identify the mean's density and the conditional independence of fixed finite collections of centered queues in the limit. On time scales of order $N$, the centered empirical mean converges to a diffusion with explicit drift and constant diffusion coefficient. These limits hold when $κ_N/N\to\infty$, along subsequences with convergent lattice phase. The diffusion limit extends to centered initial empirical measures tight in the first Wasserstein topology, with means converging in law. A short initial layer prepares the limiting family while preserving the limiting mean. Empirical approximation holds in time-integrated Wasserstein distance.

papers.title: Generalized and Convex Poincaré Inequalities via Transport-Divergence Inequalities
papers.abstract: We investigate the relationship between generalized $(q',p')$-Poincaré inequalities and transport-divergence inequalities involving $χ^q$-type divergences. Extending the classical correspondence between the $(2,2)$-Poincaré inequality and quadratic transport-$χ^2$ inequalities, we prove that a $(q',p')$-Poincaré inequality is equivalent to a transport-divergence inequality for conjugates $(p,p')$ and $(q,q')$. We then study the convex counterpart of these inequalities. Using weak barycentric optimal transport and convex order, we establish an equivalence between convex $(q',p')$-Poincaré inequalities and weak transport-divergence inequalities involving a projected $χ_q$ divergence. We further characterize the minimizers arising in this projection problem through a geometric condition on the relative density. In dimension one, we analyze the geometric consequences of $(q',p')$-Poincaré inequalities by identifying sharp conditions on the behavior of the density both at infinity and near isolated zeros. We show that when $q'>p'$, the concentration behavior becomes polynomial rather than exponential at infinity. Finally, we interpret these inequalities through the lens of optimization in Wasserstein space. In particular, the equivalence between transport-divergence and Poincaré inequalities appears as an analogue of the equivalence between quadratic growth and Polyak--Łojasiewicz inequalities in finite-dimensional optimization.

papers.title: Asymptotics of Gibbs Posterior Measures on Infinite-Dimensional Hypothesis Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove almost sure contraction rates and consistency for Gibbs posterior measures on arbitrary hypothesis spaces, in general infinite dimensional, under dependent data, nonadditive and time-dependent losses and learning rates, misspecified models, and unattainable minimisers of the limiting objective. In particular, we develop a novel proof approach in contraction rate theory by studying the asymptotics of Gibbs measures through Lorentz spaces, real interpolation theory, and Laplace transforms dispensing with testing or variational formulations which are unavailable in the considered generality. As a consequence we obtain almost sure contraction rates for dominated Bayes and fractional Bayes posterior measures in the same generality, extending existing theory on misspecified Bayesian inference. Furthermore, we demonstrate our theoretical results on novel applications to Gibbs posteriors for Dirichlet process priors with a nonadditive Wasserstein metric loss function under ergodic, non-Markovian observables.

papers.title: Nonsense rank correlations between independent random walks
papers.abstract: Yule's nonsense correlation persists for Spearman's rho and Kendall's tau between independent random walks. Neither coefficient concentrates at zero as the sample size grows. For centred random walks with finite increment variances, we derive a universal joint limit expressed through Brownian occupation functionals. Integral formulas give limiting variances of approximately 0.222 and 0.108, respectively, below the Pearson value of 0.241. Rank correlations thus reduce the limiting dispersion on their respective coefficient scales. We prove that both marginal limits have symmetric densities and represent them exactly as limits of polynomial densities determined by Gaussian moment integrals. Spearman's conventional t test and Kendall's normal approximation are asymptotically invalid, with rejection probabilities tending to one under process independence.

papers.title: The Sum of Leaf Weights in the Minimum Spanning Tree of the Complete Graph
papers.abstract: Let $G_n$ be a random weighted complete graph on $n$ vertices, where edges have i.i.d. $\text{Unif}(0,1)$ weights. Let $T_n$ be the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) of $G_n$. The expected weight of $T_n$ is known to converge to $ζ(3) = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{k^3}$ (Frieze 1985). We investigate the sum of weights of edges incident to the leaves of $T_n$, denoting this quantity by $L_n$. We give tight upper and lower bounds on $\mathbb{E}[L_n]$ and determine its limit as $n$ diverges, leveraging typical behavior of sparse Erdős--Rényi random graphs. We also establish concentration of $L_n$ around $\mathbb{E}[L_n]$ and almost sure convergence to this value. These results directly yield substantial improvements to state-of-the-art bounds for two important variants of the MST problem: (1) an improved upper bound on the weight of the optimal random instance Steiner tree, as studied by Bollobás, Gamarnik, Riordan, and Sudakov (2004); and (2) an improvement over the upper bound for the Probabilistic Minimum Spanning Tree, introduced by Bertsimas (1988).

papers.title: Laplacian Eigenvectors of Generically Weighted Graphs Have Pairwise Distinct Coordinates
papers.abstract: Poignard, Pereira and Pade conjectured that, for a generic choice of the nonzero weights of a given graph, the Fiedler vector of the weighted Laplacian has pairwise distinct coordinates. We give a proof that also covers every nonconstant eigenvector. For each connected graph on n vertices we construct a nonzero homogeneous polynomial with integer coefficients in the edge weights, of degree n(n-1)(n^2-n+2)/4, which vanishes at a positive weighting exactly when the Laplacian has a repeated eigenvalue, an eigenvector with a zero coordinate, or a nonconstant eigenvector with two equal coordinates. The exceptional weights therefore lie in an algebraic hypersurface, which gives structural genericity in the sense of Poignard, Pereira and Pade; algebraically independent weights are never exceptional, and there are good integer weights not exceeding the degree plus one. The polynomial is a product of Krylov determinants. Its nonvanishing follows by induction on trees: when a leaf is attached with a small weight, a cut identity gives the first-order profile of the new eigenvector and separates the coordinates that coincide in the limit. Exact small cases show that exceptional weightings need not be symmetric.

papers.title: Efficient scheduling of particle annihilation for long-time Wigner simulations
papers.abstract: Particle annihilation (PA) plays an indispensable role in alleviating the numerical sign problem in long-time simulations with the Wigner branching random walk (WBRW) method. However, the effect of PA frequency on long-time accuracy remains poorly understood, leaving its choice largely empirical. To provide systematic guidance for PA scheduling, we establish an overall error estimate for PA through a uniform mesh, separating WBRW variance, resampling variance and squared bias. The analysis shows that, beyond merely controlling particle growth, PA replaces the exponential-in-time variance bound with a linear-in-time bound, thereby alleviating the numerical sign problem. It also reveals bias-variance trade-off induced by PA frequency: frequent PA limits variance but can increase accumulated bias. More importantly, building on the newfound error structure, we propose a variance-constrained cost optimization strategy for adaptive PA scheduling across several PA methods. An intrinsic-time reparameterization provides a common clock for variance control, PA scheduling, and branching dynamics under time-dependent potentials. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical variance behavior and bias-variance trade-off, and results of our schedule populate the low-cost regime of the empirical Pareto frontier objecting to balance accuracy and efficiency.

papers.title: Triples in matroid circuits
papers.abstract: We prove that, if $X$ is a four-element independent set in a vertically $5$-connected representable matroid $M$, then either there is a circuit of $M$ that contains at least three elements of $X$, or there is a representation $A$ of $M$ such that each column of $A$ has at most two non-zero elements and each of the columns indexed by $X$ has exactly one non-zero element. We also prove a version of this result without the connectivity assumptions.

papers.title: \(A_α\)-Wronskian Vertices of Paths and Controllability of Path-Rooted Products
papers.abstract: For a graph \(G\) with adjacency and degree matrices \(A(G)\) and \(D(G)\), set \(A_α(G)=αD(G)+(1-α)A(G)\) for \(0\leqα<1\). Using Chebyshev polynomials and a theorem of Conway and Jones, we classify the \(A_α\)-Wronskian vertices of every path \(P_n\), \(n\geq2\) (equivalently, the standard basis vectors cyclic for \(A_α(P_n)\)). The central vertex of an odd-order path is never Wronskian; for every other vertex, we determine an explicit finite set of algebraic exceptional parameters. These sets contain no rational parameters other than \(0\) and \(1/2\), for which the adjacency and signless Laplacian cases are characterized by gcd criteria. For even-order paths rooted at either central vertex, we explicitly evaluate the root resultant and the walk-determinant polynomial in the rooted-product factorization. The resulting controllability criterion combines \(A_α\)-controllability of the base graph with at most three explicit spectral exclusions. For each parameter, one of two fixed complementary base graphs yields controllable products for every even-order path and both central roots. For \(1/2\leqα<1\), algebraic conjugates further simplify the spectral test for general rooted products.

papers.title: Peak state transfer in trees and the cost of distance
papers.abstract: There is peak state transfer between vertices $u$ and $v$ in a graph $G$ if there exists a time $t$ for which $|(\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm i t M})_{u,v}|$ saturates the triangle inequality imposed by its spectral decomposition and $M$ is either the adjacency or Laplacian matrix. We show that peak state transfer at distance $d$ requires $\frac{d^3}{24}(1 + o(1))$ edges in the adjacency case, $Ω(d^2)$ edges in the Laplacian case, and that the leading coefficient in the former is tight. We find a family of graphs with Laplacian peak state transfer at distance $d$ and $Θ(d^5)$ edges, showing that peak state transfer is achievable in a polynomial graph size. In contrast, Laplacian perfect state transfer costs at least $Ω(2^{d/2})$ edges when the distance partition of vertices around one vertex is almost equitable. Finally, we show that Laplacian peak state transfer in trees requires $Ω(d!)$ edges, and we characterize all trees of diameter $\leq 4$ admitting Laplacian peak state transfer, thus answering a pair of questions posed by Coutinho, Guo, and Schmeits.

papers.title: On Pairwise Independent and Strongly Correlated Random Variables
papers.abstract: Characterizing joint distributions that maximize the centered third-order moment under prescribed marginal distributions and pairwise independence has various statistical applications. This problem can be formulated as a multistochastic optimal transport problem. In this work, we generalize the results on the $(3,2)$-multistochastic Monge-Kantorovich problem to cost functions of the form $c(x,y,z)=f(x)f(y)f(z)$, where $f$ is defined on $[0,1]$ through dyadic expansions: $f(x)=\sum_{i\geq 1} a_i x_i$, with $x_i\in\{0,1\}$. Under summability and domination conditions on the coefficients, we show that an optimal transport plan is concentrated on the Sierpinski tetrahedron. We also characterize mixtures of geometric coefficient sequences through Hausdorff moment sequences and construct a recursive dual solution with its integral representation for costs with geometric coefficients.

papers.title: Adapted transport inequalities in continuous time
papers.abstract: Given a strong solution $X$ to a stochastic differential equation (SDE), we establish sufficient conditions under which $\text{Law}(X)$ satisfies an adapted quadratic transport cost inequality (AQTCI) with respect to the semimartingale adapted Wasserstein distance. When the drift and diffusion coefficients are Markovian, we further show that the AQTCI tensorizes in a dimension-free manner. As a corollary, we show that various stochastic control problems, e.g. optimal stopping and mean-variance portfolio selection, are stable under bounded, measurable drift perturbations. Additionally, we derive concentration inequalities (with respect to certain dynamic risk measures) for stochastic integrals $\int H_s dX_s$ and deduce appropriate bounds on their tail behavior. Furthermore, using the functional Itô formula, we show that the AQTCI for $\text{Law}(X)$ allows one to deduce classical transport inequalities for $\text{Law}(F(X))$ even when $F$ is not Lipschitz on path space. Finally, we give sufficient conditions for $\text{Law}(X)$ to satisfy AQTCIs when $X$ is a solution to a scalar fractional SDE or stochastic Volterra equation.

papers.title: Characterisation of first passage locations for two-dimensional lattice random walks
papers.abstract: Consider a diagonal random walk $(X_n,Y_n)$ on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with transition probabilities depending only on the second coordinate. We characterise the distributions of first passage locations, $X(τ_a)$, where $τ_a$ is the first time $Y_n$ reaches level $a$. We obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for a given distribution to be realised as a rescaled first passage location from some starting level. The proof extends Bondesson's method for one-dimensional first passage times. It combines a transformation of generating functions based on Pick functions with a construction using barriers. We also study maximal representations of generating functions of first passage locations and show that analogous converse results for standard and honeycomb random walks require additional restrictions.

papers.title: Tightness of bulk crossing heights for the planar discrete Gaussian free field
papers.abstract: Let $φ_N$ be the planar discrete Gaussian free field in $[-2N,2N]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$, with zero boundary condition imposed by killing the associated simple random walk on exit. We consider the least height $H_N$ at which the two-sided level set $\{|φ_N|\leq a\}$ contains a nearest-neighbor left--right crossing of $[-N,N]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$. We prove that $(H_N)_{N\geq1}$ is tight, uniformly over all box sizes. More precisely, for every $a\geq0$ and $N\geq1$, \[ Φ\!\left(-a\sqrt{\frac{2}{\log2}}\right) \leq\mathbb{P}(H_N>a) \leq4\exp\!\left\{-2^{-29}\frac{a^2}{\log(2+a)}\right\}, \] where $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. The upper bound yields uniform polynomial moments and a uniform exponential moment of $H_N^2/\log(2+H_N)$. For the upper bound, we compare a marked loop-soup exploration with a graph in which independent site variables open incoming edges. We then estimate connections in a massive field using two auxiliary vertices and bound the Gaussian remainder when the mass is removed. The lower bound uses a Gaussian translation inequality and a square-shell estimate for the Dirichlet energy, without using the massive-field argument. In particular, a height independent of $N$ gives any prescribed crossing probability below one, whereas every fixed finite height has a uniformly positive failure probability.

papers.title: IsaGraphLib: Formally Verified Efficient Graph Algorithms in Isabelle/HOL
papers.abstract: We present a library of formally verified graph algorithms in Isabelle/HOL. The library covers the main problems of combinatorial optimisation on graphs: reachability, shortest paths, minimum spanning trees, matching, maximum flow, and minimum-cost flow. The algorithms in the library use most of the standard algorithm design techniques: graph search, greedy algorithms on matroids, dynamic programming, augmenting paths, blossom contraction, blocking flows, push-relabel, scaling, the primal-dual method, randomisation, and certificate checking. The library has adaptors between different types of graphs (directed, undirected, multigraphs), which allow results to be reused. Each algorithm is verified independently of its data structures, and the main algorithms are refined to efficient imperative implementations, from which we generate code in Standard ML, Scala, and Go. We developed parts of the library with large language models (LLMs), improved the quality of their proofs with a method based on statistics of our own proofs, and labelled which parts were developed by humans, by LLMs, or collaboratively. We perform a detailed experimental analysis of representative algorithms in our library, comparing it with state-of-the-art mainstream libraries, showing that our implementations are practical.

papers.title: Optimal mixing of random-to-random shuffling on linear extensions
papers.abstract: Uniform sampling of linear extensions is a basic problem in randomized algorithms and the study of finite posets. We prove that the random-to-random shuffle of Ayyer, Schilling, and Thiéry mixes in $O(n\log n+n\log(1/\varepsilon))$ steps on every $n$-element poset, establishing their conjectured mixing order. With constant-time order queries, this gives an $\varepsilon$-approximate uniform sampler using $O(n^2(\log n+\log(1/\varepsilon)))$ elementary operations after preprocessing. The proof establishes relative-entropy contraction by a factor $1-1/n$ for the promotion half-step. Consequently, the uniform extended-promotion chain has the same mixing order. We represent complete promotion scans as reflected coordinate paths in the order polytope and prove that a convex potential with gradients in the same polytope has diagonal Hessian mass at most one along each path. Applying this estimate to an optimal transport potential yields a sharp entropy factorization for every finite-entropy input. Linearization also gives the spectral-gap lower bound $(n+1)/n^2$.

papers.title: Sharp Gaussian Approximation for Q-Learning
papers.abstract: Gaussian approximation provides a foundation for online statistical inference in reinforcement learning. We establish sharp non-asymptotic Gaussian approximation rates in Wasserstein distance for asynchronous Q-learning with Polyak-Ruppert averaging. We prove an upper bound of $\widetilde{O}(n^{-1/4})$, where $n$ is the number of iterations, together with a matching lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Q-learning is more challenging to analyze than linear stochastic approximation due to the nonlinearity of the Bellman operator. Asynchronous updates introduce further challenges due to Markovian noise. Our analysis separates the errors from Bellman nonlinearity, Markovian noise, and the finite-sample covariance discrepancy. In particular, we show that Markovian noise induces an unavoidable bias even when the Bellman operator is linear. The trade-off between this bias and the covariance discrepancy determines the convergence rate. We further extend our analysis to the synchronous setting and establish a sharp rate of $\widetilde{O}(n^{-1/2})$.

papers.title: On the multiplicity of the Laplacian eigenvalue 1 of a graph
papers.abstract: A connected graph $G$ with $n\ge 2$ vertices and $\varepsilon$ edges is called a \emph{$k$-cyclic graph} if $k=\varepsilon-n+1$. The Laplacian matrix is defined as $L(G)=D(G)-A(G)$, where $D(G)$ is the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees and $A(G)$ is the adjacency matrix of $G$. Let $m_{G}(1)$ be the multiplicity of the Laplacian eigenvalue $1$ of $G$. In this paper, we show that for fixed integers $n\ge \big\lceil\frac{3+\sqrt{8k+1}} {2}\big\rceil$ and $k\geq0$, if $G$ is a $k$-cyclic graph of order $n$, then \begin{equation*} \displaystyle m_{G}(1)\leq n-\big\lceil\frac{3+\sqrt{8k+1}} {2}\big\rceil \end{equation*} and moreover, we completely characterize all extremal graphs attained the upper bound.

papers.title: Martingale and signed diffusive optimal transport: geodesics and gradient flows
papers.abstract: In signed diffusive transport, a path of probability densities $ρ_t$ on the circle and a momentum $m_t$ satisfy $\partial_tρ=\partial_{xx}m$, and the cost of the path is the action $\int_0^1\int m^2/(2ρ)\,dx\,dt$. The diffusivity $m/ρ$ is an unknown of this variational problem and can take either sign. On the real line, the constraint $m\ge0$ gives the martingale Benamou-Brenier problem of Huesmann and Trevisan. We study geodesics and minimizing movements, which discretize gradient flows. For signed geodesics, we prove the $Γ$-convergence of the time-discrete problems for all probability endpoints, and of the fully discrete Fourier-grid problems as the space and time meshes tend to zero independently, without a positive lower bound on the densities. For a modified Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto (JKO) scheme on the torus, we prove convergence along subsequences to a weak solution of a fourth-order equation, the Derrida-Lebowitz-Speer-Spohn equation for the entropy in dimension one, under the assumption that the densities of the scheme stay above a positive constant on every finite time interval. In dimension one, the normalized minimum values of a discretization with nonnegative momentum and of a discretization by martingale couplings with a fourth-moment cost converge to the same martingale transport cost, and we identify the limit of the minimizing movements with nonnegative momentum for potential energies with bounded second and third derivatives. We compute geodesics and modified JKO trajectories by Douglas-Rachford splitting and by an interior-point method, and bound the optimization errors of selected solutions by dual lower bounds evaluated in interval arithmetic. The computed geodesics approach zero density near the points where the diffusivity changes sign, and along computed trajectories of the modified JKO scheme the density minimum can fall below its initial value.

papers.title: Cogirth-Strength Ratios and Matroid Rank Reduction
papers.abstract: In the rank-$p$ reduction problem, we are given a matroid with nonnegative element weights and seek a minimum-weight set of elements whose deletion lowers the rank by at least $p$. For graphic matroids, this is the minimum $(p+1)$-cut problem. Chekuri, Quanrud, and Xu developed a tree-packing algorithm for minimum $k$-cut, which relies on the fact that the minimum cut of a graph is at most twice its strength, the value of a maximum fractional packing of spanning trees. We generalize this approach from graphs to matroids. The matroid analogue of the minimum cut is the cogirth, the minimum weight of a cocircuit, and the analogue of graph strength is matroid strength, the value of a maximum fractional packing of bases. We show that if every matroid in a deletion-closed class has cogirth at most $d$ times its strength, then for every $p$, the natural linear programming relaxation of rank-$p$ reduction is within a factor of $d$ of the optimum. As a result, repeatedly deleting a minimum-weight cocircuit gives a $d$-approximation, and an optimal solution can be found deterministically in $n^{(2d-1)p+O(1)}$ time on $n$ elements. For graphs, $d=2$ and our framework specializes to the tree-packing approach. As applications, we bound the cogirth-strength ratio for two broad classes, and both bounds are tight. For quasi-graphic matroids, which include graphic, bicircular, frame, and lifted-graphic matroids, the ratio is at most $2$ for all weights, giving a $2$-approximation and an exact $n^{3p+O(1)}$-time algorithm. For $(k,\ell)$-count matroids of hypergraphs with $0\le \ell\le k$ and edge size at most $s$, the ratio is at most $ks$ under unit weights. This gives a $ks$-approximation and an exact $n^{(2ks-1)p+O(1)}$-time algorithm for unweighted rank-$p$ reduction.

papers.title: Matroid Parity Meets Vertex Splitting
papers.abstract: A vertex split replaces a vertex by two non-adjacent descendants and partitions its incident edges between them. We study exclusive $\ell$-shallow splitting, where each original vertex has at most $\ell+1$ descendants, with the aim of obtaining a forest, a pseudoforest, or a cluster graph. We consider two natural objectives: minimizing the total number of split operations and minimizing the number of original vertices that are split. Our main conceptual contribution is a connection between vertex splitting and matroid parity. For both forests and pseudoforests, we give a characterization of feasible splitting sequences that leads, via weighted linear matroid parity, to polynomial-time algorithms for minimizing the number of split vertices when $\ell=2$. These algorithms are complemented by NP-hardness for every fixed $\ell\ge3$; for pseudoforests, hardness holds even on graphs of maximum degree four. The total number of split operations behaves differently: for both sparse target classes, this objective is polynomial-time solvable for every $\ell$, using matroid intersection. For cluster graphs, both objectives admit linear-time algorithms when $\ell=1$ and are NP-hard for every fixed $\ell\ge2$. Together, these results identify how the target class, the local splitting bound, and the choice of objective determine the complexity of vertex splitting.

papers.title: The $E_6$-Grassmannian, its minuscule Coxeter matroids, and the lines on a cubic surface
papers.abstract: We study the minuscule Coxeter matroids of type $E_6$, whose ground set is the set of 27 lines on a smooth cubic surface. We characterize them by a tritangent exchange property and classify them into 230 orbits under the Weyl group. Every nonempty matroidal stratum of the $E_6$-Grassmannian is an open subscheme of a torus, and all orbits but one are realizable over every infinite field. Finally, we compute the tropical $E_6$-Grassmannian and its 60 classes of toric degenerations. This is an extended abstract for a forthcoming paper.

papers.title: The elephant random walk with proportionally growing recent memory
papers.abstract: In this work, we study an elephant random walk with recent restricted memory, where at step $n$ the elephant remembers only the last $m_n=\max\{\lfloor cn\rfloor,1\}$ steps for $c\in(0,1)$. We show that the random walk undergoes a phase transition at the critical point $p_c=(3+\sqrt{1-c})/4$, which depends on the memory proportion $c$. For $0<p<p_c$, $S_n/\sqrt{n}$ is asymptotically normal; for $p=p_c$, $S_n/\sqrt{n\log n}$ is asymptotically normal; and for $p_c<p<1$, $S_n/n^ρ$ converges almost surely and in $L^2$ to a random variable for some constant $ρ\in (1/2, 1)$. This phase transition differs from that of the classical elephant random walk and its remote-memory counterpart, both of which have the same fixed critical point $3/4$.

papers.title: Domains of attraction of quasi-stationary distributions for an absorbed random walk
papers.abstract: We study a continuous-time random walk on the positive integers, killed at zero, where the downward rate $a$ and upward rate $b$ satisfy $a>b>0$. Its quasi-stationary distributions form a one-parameter family. We show that if the initial distribution $(m_n)_{n\geq 1}$ is strictly positive and satisfies $m_{n+1}/m_n\to r$, where $(b/a)^{1/2}<r<1$, then its conditional distribution given survival converges in total variation to the corresponding nonminimal quasi-stationary distribution. We obtain asymptotic equivalents for the joint probabilities of position and survival, and for the survival probability itself. We also give a moment condition under which the minimal quasi-stationary distribution is selected. Finally, we construct an initial distribution whose successive-term ratios do not converge but whose conditional distribution nevertheless converges to a nonminimal quasi-stationary distribution. Thus the ratio condition is sufficient but not necessary.

papers.title: Quasi-product and multiplicative Markov measures Radon-Nikodym problem, random walks: the free group case
papers.abstract: The purpose of this paper is a conceptual clarification of the role of a special class of measures on topological Markov chains - multiplicative Markov measures - in the context of random walks. It is achieved by combining the interpretation of multiplicative Markov measures on the boundary of a free group as the unique solutions of the Radon - Nikodym problem for product cocycles of the boundary action and the fact that the Radon - Nikodym cocycle of the harmonic measure of a nearest neighbour random walk on a free group is a product one.

papers.title: Well-Posedness of Semimartingale Optimal Transport with Partial Marginal Constraints for Model Calibration
papers.abstract: We study the well-posedness and stability of a semimartingale optimal transport problem with partial marginal constraints at several maturities, motivated by the calibration of financial models to finitely many option prices. We connect its probabilistic and Eulerian formulations within the Benamou--Brenier framework. Under convex-duality assumptions, we establish strong duality for every price vector in the extended-value sense and existence of a primal optimizer whenever the value is finite. Under additional PDE assumptions, we establish dual attainment on the relative interior of the admissible price set, together with uniqueness of the primal optimizer. Under further non-degeneracy assumptions, we show that this price set has nonempty interior, on which the dual optimizer is unique and depends locally Lipschitz continuously on the prices. The analysis combines convex methods with regularity and local strong convexity results for Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman solution maps established in a companion paper. For a fixed deterministic initial state, we also prove continuity of the optimal law on path space in the adapted Wasserstein distance of order two as prices vary within this interior. This stability concerns the optimizer over the full admissible class of semimartingale laws, allowing characteristics that depend on the past. The framework accommodates bounded uniformly continuous payoffs, including European puts in log-price coordinates, without payoff regularization or spatial truncation.

papers.title: Guerra Interpolation and Optimal Transport: Kantorovich Bounds, Brenier Maps and the Replicon
papers.abstract: Since Guerra's work, mean-field spin glasses have been studied through Hamilton--Jacobi equations. Here, using the Curie--Weiss and the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick models as prototypical examples, we show that his celebrated interpolation method is itself an optimal transport computation. After a linear change of variables the finite-$N$ pressure becomes an action $u$ with $\partial_t u = -A/2$ and $\partial_x u = -B$, where $B^2 \le A$, so $u$ is a classical subsolution of $\partial_t u+\frac12(\partial_x u)^2 \le 0$. Integrating along a straight segment gives Guerra's sum rule, and dropping its remainder makes $u(0,\cdot)$ and $u(t,\cdot)$ an admissible pair for the dual Kantorovich problem with quadratic cost. For the Curie--Weiss model and $t > 0$, $T_t(y) = y-t\tanh y$ is an optimal transport map from every source with finite first moment if and only if $t \le 1$, and the Kantorovich potentials are the limiting pressures. For the replica-symmetric Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model, the cavity map is injective on the physical half-line and the curvature of its Brenier potential is the longitudinal eigenvalue, which exceeds the replicon eigenvalue $Λ_{\mathrm{AT}}$: transport of Dirac masses does not detect the de Almeida--Thouless line. The replicon appears along the $\mathcal{W}_2$ geodesic that splits a Dirac mass into two atoms, as the second variation of a second-order surrogate of the two-atom Parisi functional. From a Dirac initial datum, Guerra's $K$-step bound takes Hopf--Lax form, and the Parisi formula becomes a Hopf--Lax formula over atomic measures. With a $\mathcal{W}_1$-Lipschitz bound for its initial datum, proved by comparing Cole--Hopf layers, we let $K\to\infty$ and recover at Dirac data the Hopf--Lax form of the Parisi formula due to Mourrat and to Mourrat and Panchenko, with a rate for equal-mass approximations.

papers.title: Refined random matrix conjectures for zeros of $p$-adic $L$-functions
papers.abstract: We make and test the conjecture that for $p$-adic $L$-functions associated to quadratic Dirichlet characters and their Teichmüller twists, all local statistics of zeros in the unit disk match those of $p$-adic random matrix eigenvalues. This generalizes the case of the number of zeros in the unit disk previously conjectured by Ellenberg-Jain-Venkatesh, which was well-supported by numerics, as well as the case of the discriminant, where their numerics were more ambiguous. Using recent random matrix results on local statistics of eigenvalues, we make the random matrix prediction explicit for many statistics, analogous to local densities and pair-correlations in the complex setting. To test these, we compute data on $p$-adic $L$-functions for characters of conductor up to $10^7$, and for certain statistics in windows above $10^{10}$. We find good agreement with the new random matrix predictions for these statistics, as well as for the discriminant.

papers.title: Enumeration of Cospectral Graphs with Respect to the Average Flow Matrix
papers.abstract: A graph is said to be determined by the spectrum of a graph-associated matrix if no nonisomorphic graph shares the same spectrum with it. In this paper, we introduce the average flow matrix of a connected graph and study its spectral properties. We investigate its effectiveness in distinguishing graphs by carrying out a computational enumeration of connected graphs having a cospectral mate with respect to this matrix up to order 10. Our computations show that every connected graph on at most 10 vertices is determined by the spectrum of the average flow matrix. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first graph-associated matrix for which the spectrum distinguishes all connected graphs of order at most 10.

papers.title: Construction and discrete approximation of the renormalized fractional parabolic Anderson model
papers.abstract: For a directed polymer in a discrete fractional Gaussian environment, we identify the scaling limit of its partition field with the renormalized Stratonovich solution of the one-dimensional parabolic Anderson model with fractional noise and flat initial condition. The underlying walk is simple and symmetric, and the temporal and spatial Hurst indices satisfy $H_0>\frac12$, $\frac12\le H_1<1$ and $2H_0+H_1<2$. After an explicit deterministic normalization, the interpolated partition field converges in law in $C_{\rm loc}([0,\infty)\times\R)$, with convergence of all finite moments of its supremum norm on compacts. We construct the limiting field directly by smoothing the noise in the equation and subtracting the corresponding stationary counterterm. The classical solutions converge in $L^p(Ω;C(\mathcal K))$ for every $1\le p<\infty$ and every compact space-time rectangle $\mathcal K$, including those that meet the initial line $t=0$. For $2H_0+H_1>\frac53$, the limit agrees with the solution that Chen, Ouyang, Tindel and the author constructed using regularity structures. The construction also covers the new range $\frac32<2H_0+H_1\le\frac53$. The proofs rely on Feynman-Kac representations and on estimates and invariance principles for weighted self- and mutual intersections of random walks and Brownian motions, together with uniform increment estimates and Gaussian hypercontractivity.

papers.title: From Butson Hadamard switching to graph switching and back
papers.abstract: Switching is a local operation that preserves specified properties of a combinatorial object. It has been used to derive constructions of inequivalent Hadamard matrices and nonisomorphic cospectral graphs. In this paper we investigate the relation between these constructions for real and Butson Hadamard matrices. We show that, while equivalent matrices have isomorphic associated graphs, the converse can fail for Butson matrices. We prove that a character decomposition determines the graph spectrum from the singular values of entrywise powers. For prime phase, we also observe that the spectrum depends only on the order and phase; for composite phase, a switching preserving the Butson property can change it. We show that Orrick's closed-quadruple and Hall-set switchings correspond to Wang-Qiu-Hu switching, up to graph isomorphism. Going in the other direction, we characterise when the Godsil-McKay and Wang-Qiu-Hu reflections preserve the Butson property and give phase-multiplicity conditions for the corresponding graph switchings. Finally we also relate block switching to cyclic graph switching under a phase-balance condition, automatic at prime phase. These results provide a basis for transferring tools and techniques between matrix switching and graph switching.

papers.title: Rank Functions of Flag Matroids with Applications to Order-Neutral Submodular Valuations
papers.abstract: We provide a rank function axiomatization for flag matroids and show that it is cryptomorphic to the definition of flag matroids as a sequence of matroid quotients. Afterwards, we present some applications of flag matroid rank functions by providing solutions to selected problems. In particular, we discuss connections between flag matroids and submodular valuations in computational economics by showing that rank functions of flag matroids of length $k$ are precisely the same as $\{0, 1, \dots, k\}$-order-neutral submodular valuations. We then prove that $v:2^E\to \mathbb{R}$ is an order-neutral submodular valuation if and only if $v$ can be written as $v(X) = b|X| + \sum_{i=1}^l c_ir_{N_i}(X), \quad b \in \mathbb{R}, c_i > 0$, where $N_{i+1}$ is a quotient of $N_i$. Doing so allows us to prove that every order-neutral submodular valuation is a gross-substitute valuation and that not every order-neutral submodular valuation is a Rado valuation. Furthermore, we prove that if $|E|\geq 3$, then a set $A$ is a Sidon set if and only if all $A$-submodular valuations are order-neutral, if and only if all $A$-submodular valuations are gross-substitute valuations.

papers.title: Nonsense nonlinear correlations between independent random walks
papers.abstract: Sample distance correlation can remain large between independent random walks. For centred walks with independent, identically distributed increments of finite, positive variance, we prove convergence in distribution to the distance correlation of the joint occupation measure of two independent Brownian paths. This universal limit lies strictly between zero and one almost surely and has full support on the unit interval. We calculate the expected squared distance covariance of the limiting measure and show that ordinary permutation calibration rejects independence with probability tending to one at every fixed nominal level. Gaussian simulations illustrate the persistent dispersion of random-walk correlations and the failure of permutation calibration.

papers.title: Resistance-regular graphs need not be regular
papers.abstract: A connected graph is resistance-regular if the sum of the effective resistances from a vertex to all other vertices does not depend on the vertex, or equivalently if the Moore-Penrose inverse of its Laplacian has constant diagonal. Walk-regular graphs have this property, and Zhou, Wang and Bu asked in 2016 whether every resistance-regular graph is regular, a question that also arises in the study of graphs with constant resistance curvature. We answer this question in the negative and examine both what resistance-regularity forces and how far from regular such graphs can be. On the spectral side, we prove that a connected graph is walk-regular if and only if the first $m-1$ powers of its Laplacian pseudoinverse have constant diagonal, where $m$ is the number of distinct nonzero Laplacian eigenvalues. Because resistance-regularity constrains only the first power, it forces regularity when $m\le2$ and allows at most two vertex degrees when $m=3$. Any non-regular resistance-regular graph has minimum degree at least $3$ and a connected complement, and an exhaustive computer search shows that it must have at least $13$ vertices. For every even $p\ge4$, we construct a resistance-regular graph on $4p$ vertices with degrees $2p-2$ and $2p-1$, obtaining closed formulas for its Laplacian spectrum and for all pairwise effective resistances. Using module blow-ups, we then construct $n$-vertex resistance-regular graphs whose two degrees differ by $(\sqrt{4n+1}-5)/4$ for infinitely many $n$, as well as examples with three and four distinct degrees, whereas the maximum and minimum degrees of any resistance-regular graph on $n$ vertices differ by less than $n/2$. We close by conjecturing that in a resistance-regular graph the sum of squared resistances at a vertex increases strictly with its degree.

papers.title: On the continuity of martingale optimal transport in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: We investigate qualitative and quantitative continuity of martingale optimal transport under perturbations of both marginals in dimensions $d\geq2$. We assume that each pair of marginals admits a reference martingale coupling whose density relative to the product of its marginals is bounded above and away from zero, uniformly along the sequence. If the limiting target measure is not carried by a hyperplane, we prove continuity under $W_1$-convergence for continuous costs of at most linear growth, assuming only finite first moments. For Lipschitz costs, a uniform $p$-moment bound on the targets, $p>1$, yields an explicit stability estimate with exponent $(1-1/p)/2$; uniformly bounded target supports give exponent $1/2$. The proof constructs a correction of couplings with small martingale bias while preserving both marginals. Truncated moment corrections allow the target measure to have unbounded support. The construction also shows that every martingale coupling of the limiting marginals can be approximated in $W_1$ by martingale couplings of the approximating marginals. We also discuss counterexamples showing that neither the uniform density condition nor non-degeneracy of the limiting target measure can be omitted in general.

papers.title: Price-impact Martingale optimal transport
papers.abstract: Martingale optimal transport (MOT) provides model-independent bounds for option prices calibrated to vanilla options, assuming frictionless trading in the underlying. In this work, we consider the case where dynamic trading incurs quadratic temporary price impact. First, we prove a duality result for the superhedging price. In particular, the primal of the duality relaxes the strict martingale constraint by penalizing the deviation from a specific martingale. Second, for one asset and one trading period, we interpret this price-impact martingale optimal transport (PIMOT) as a weak optimal transport (WOT) problem, and provide a characterization in the spirit of Wasserstein projection. Finally, we justify that PIMOT is an interpolation between MOT and classical optimal transport (OT), and derive the convergence rate to both sides. Numerical examples with SPX option data show how the price bounds per claim depend on the order size.

papers.title: Mass gap for the fractional $Φ^4_2$ model
papers.abstract: We present a new, simple and self-contained technique for proving a mass gap for Euclidean quantum field theories in the high-temperature regime using the stochastic quantisation approach. As an application, we establish exponential decay of spatial correlations for the fractional $Φ^4$ model on the plane in the Wick-ordering regime. The key idea is to analyse the propagation of perturbations using the linearised stochastic quantisation equation. Spatial propagation is controlled by an auxiliary random walk, while the potentially destabilising effect of the renormalised nonlinearity is controlled by combining dissipative energy estimates for the nonlinear dynamic with the Boué-Dupuis variational formula.

papers.title: On the maximum of Poissonian log-correlated fields
papers.abstract: We consider stationary log-correlated random fields of the form \[ X_n(t):= \sum_{j\le n} f(e^{τ_j} t+ v_{j})\,,\quad t\in \mathbb{R} \] for a centered 1-periodic analytic function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, where $(τ_j)_{j\ge1}$ are the arrival times of a rate-1 Poisson process on $\mathbb{R}_+$ and $(v_j)_{j\ge1}$ are iid uniform random variables in $[0,1)$. We show that with high probability, \[ \max_{t\in[-1,1]}X_n(t) = c_1 n + c_2 τ_n- (c_3+o(1))\log n \] where $c_1,c_2,c_3$ are positive constants depending on $f$. In particular, the random frequency $τ_n$ produces a central limit fluctuation of order $\sqrt{n}$, together with a logarithmic correction different from the ubiquitous Bramson correction for models with strong comparisons to Gaussian fields, such as homogeneous branching random walks and log-characteristic polynomials of C$β$E matrices. Our proof makes a connection with branching random walks in random time-environment, where coarse-scale fluctuations of the arrival times $τ_j$ play the role of a quenched random environment, and fine-scale fluctuations are leveraged to establish a branching decorrelation structure. We conjecture analogous asymptotics for the characteristic polynomials of random permutation matrices, and expect the same mechanism to arise in other Poissonian fields such as characteristic polynomials of sparse random matrices.

papers.title: Annihilation versus anchoring of a topologically charged pair on a perforated two-dimensional surface
papers.abstract: Two independent random walks of opposite topological charge move on the discrete torus $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^2$, which contains $k$ well-separated holes. The walks annihilate when they come within a core distance of each other, and each walk is anchored when it first touches a hole. We prove that the probability of annihilation before anchoring converges to $w_0/(w_0+\sum_j w_j)$, where the weights are explicit and depend only logarithmically on the sizes of the core and of the holes; for point-like core and holes, the limit is $1/(1+k)$. We then prove a fate theorem: the pair either terminates or ends as two opposite charges anchored on two different holes, with probability $(k-1)/(k+1)$ in the point-like case, and the hosting pair $\{j,l\}$ is chosen with probability proportional to $w_jw_l$. The proof combines an abstract competition lemma for rare sets in reversible Markov chains with sharp two-dimensional Green's function estimates.

papers.title: When Elements Fail: Weighted Fault-Tolerant Matroid Bases
papers.abstract: Given a rank-\(r\) matroid on \(n\) elements with nonnegative costs and a partition into safe and vulnerable elements, we seek a minimum-cost set that spans after every deletion of at most \(k\) selected vulnerable elements. We resolve several open questions posed by Bentert, Fomin, Golovach, and Morelle (ESA 2025) concerning weighted costs, nonuniform failures, and explicitly specified failure scenarios. To this end, we develop two compression methods. For matroids given by an independence oracle, weighted flat-avoidance representatives yield a bounded subset of the ground set containing an optimal solution and a \(2^{\mathcal{O}((r+k)^4)}n^{\mathcal{O}(1)}\)-time algorithm. This establishes fixed-parameter tractability for weighted costs and nonuniform failures simultaneously. For explicitly represented linear matroids, polynomial certificates allow us to compress families of partial solutions while preserving successful completions under all allowed failures. This yields a deterministic algorithm using \(2^{\mathcal{O}(kr(r+k)\log(r+1))}n^{\mathcal{O}(1)}\) field operations over arbitrary fields. Over fixed finite fields, a simpler reduction uses parallel classes. For explicitly listed failure scenarios, we obtain fixed-parameter algorithms parameterized by rank and the number of scenarios. In contrast, the size-budget decision version is W[1]-hard parameterized by rank and maximum scenario size, even on uniform matroids with two-element scenarios. \keywords{Matroids \and Fault tolerance \and Fixed-parameter algorithms \and Representative families}

papers.title: The spectrum of free projective geometries over finite chain rings
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{O}$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak{p}$ a prime ideal of residue order $q$, and $\mathcal{O}_r=\mathcal{O}/\mathfrak{p}^r$ which is a finite chain ring; the motivating example is $\mathbb{Z}/p^r$. The free projective geometry $\mathbb{P}^{d-1}_{fr}(\mathcal{O}_r)$ is the graph whose vertices are the nontrivial free submodules of $\mathcal{O}_r^{d}$, two of them adjacent when one strictly contains the other. For every $d$, $q$ and $r$ we reduce its adjacency matrix to explicit symmetric matrices (blocks) of size at most $d-1$. There is one block for each signature (a partition with at most $d/2$ parts, each at most $r$) and we show that every block, at every depth, is a single universal matrix $L(s,σ)$ evaluated at the number $s$ of parts of the signature $λ$ and at $σ=2rs-|λ|$. The same blocks give the spectrum of the subgraph induced on any set of levels, and for two levels this spectrum is completely explicit. All of it depends on the ring only through $q$ and $r$; in particular the subgraphs $\mathbb{P}^{d-1}_{S}$ over $\mathbb{Z}/p^r$ and over $\mathbb{F}_p[t]/(t^r)$ are isospectral for all $\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\{1,\dots,d-1\}$; together with known rigidity results of arXiv:2510.09324, this proves that they are isospectral and non-isomorphic whenever $S$ contains at least two levels, as conjectured there.

papers.title: Exact Wasserstein Convergence Rate for Conditional Empirical Measures of Killed Diffusion Processes
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a $d$-dimensional compact connected Riemannian manifold $M$ with boundary $\pp M$, and let $X_t$ be the diffusion process generated by $L:=\DD+\nn V$ for some $V\in C^2(M)$ which is killed on the boundary. For any initial distribution $ν$ which is not fully supported on $\pp M$, let $μ_t^ν$ be the conditional empirical measure for the diffusion process under the condition that the process is not yet killed at time $t$, and let $μ_0$ be the associated quasi-stationary distribution. We derive the sharp convergence rate of $μ_t^ν$ to $μ_0$ in the quadratic Wasserstein distance $\W_2$ as $t\to\infty$. In particular, if $ν(B(x,r))\asymp r^k$ for some $k\in [0,d]$ and all $r\in [0,1]$ uniformly in $x\in {\rm supp}ν$, then for large $t>0$ $$ \W_2(μ_t^ν,μ_0)\asymp_ν\begin{cases} t^{-1},&d-k<6,\\ t^{-1}\sqrt{\log t},&d-k=6,\\ t^{-\ff{d-k+2}{2(d-k-2)}},&d-k>6. \end{cases} $$ Moreover, letting $\rr_\pp(x)$ be the distance of $x$ to $\pp M$, for large $t>0$ we have $$ \W_2(μ_t^{\dd_x},μ_0)\asymp \begin{cases} t^{-1},&d\le 3,\\ t^{-1}\log (1+\rr_\pp(x)^{-1}), & d=4,\\ t^{-1} \rr_\pp(x)^{-1}, & d=5,\\ t^{-1}\sqrt{\log t} \rr_\pp(x)^{-1},&d=6,\\ t^{-\ff{d+2}{2(d-2)}}\rr_\pp(x)^{-\ff 4{d-2}},&d\ge 7. \end{cases} $$

papers.title: Asymptotic transportation cost of the optimal matching subject to different boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We establish equality between several asymptotic limits of the transportation cost between stationary random measures, with respect to the Euclidean distance cost raised to the $p$-th power, with different boundary conditions. Our approach relies on a comparison with the optimizer of the mean transportation cost between the two random measures, which is defined on the whole space. In particular we do not use any PDE techniques related to the regularity theory for optimal transport maps.

papers.title: Positivity in symplectic groups and electrical networks
papers.abstract: We study the relation between electrical positivity introduced by Lam and Pylyavskyy $[9]$ and total positivity of symplectic matrices arising from circular planar electrical networks. A particularly convenient framework for our purpose is provided by a construction of an embedding of electrical network into the positive Lagrangian Grassmannian, see Section $1.1$. Employing this technique, we demonstrate that mentioned below two types of positivity do not coincide, see Theorem $2.2$. In Section $3$ we also derive explicit rational formulas recovering the parameters of the factorization from our symplectic matrix entries and minors, and prove uniqueness under explicit nonvanishing conditions.

papers.title: Recurrence and Transience in Monotone Environments: Increasing Conductances and Growing Domains
papers.abstract: We study discrete-time random walks on a locally finite graph whose conductances are non-decreasing in time and bounded on each edge. We compare their hitting probabilities with those of the time-homogeneous walk obtained by fixing the conductances at the starting time. These estimates give proofs of two results established in greater generality by Li and Park: if the upper network is recurrent, every vertex is visited infinitely often almost surely; if the initial network is transient, the expected number of visits to each vertex is finite. In a finite domain, the difference between the two exit probabilities is bounded by the square root of the product of a capacity increment and a dual energy. We obtain a corresponding infinite-volume estimate for the probability of never hitting a given vertex. To prove these estimates, we compare two Dirichlet forms and use a contraction property of the killed transition operators. We also consider walks on increasing finite sets. On each prescribed time interval, called a plateau, the transition operator is fixed. A lower bound on transition probabilities after mixing and an upper bound on the expected number of returns give a sufficient condition for every vertex to be visited infinitely often almost surely. For uniformly elliptic lazy walks on boxes of radius $R_n$ in $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\geq3$, it is enough that $\sum_n(L_n-b_n)_+/R_n^d$ diverges, where $L_n$ is the duration of the $n$th plateau and $b_n=\lceil aR_n^2\rceil$.

papers.title: Every rank-three matroid is Z-Rayleigh
papers.abstract: We prove that every matroid of rank or corank at most three is $Z$-Rayleigh: its multivariate Tutte polynomial satisfies the Rayleigh inequalities for every positive weighting and every parameter $0<q\le1$. This settles a conjecture of Mani and answers the rank-$3$ spanning-correlation question of Cocks and the correlated-matroid question of Semple and Welsh. For simple rank-$3$ matroids, we obtain an explicit decomposition of each spanning-set Rayleigh difference into the corresponding basis Rayleigh difference, positively weighted squares, and a polynomial with nonnegative coefficients. A second identity compares the normalized multivariate Tutte Rayleigh difference with $(1-q)^2$ times the spanning-set difference, with a remainder of the form $q(1-q)R(q,x)$, where $R$ has nonnegative coefficients. The proof uses the bipartite incidence graph of the lines through two fixed elements and Wagner's theorem that rank-$3$ matroids are basis-Rayleigh. The rank bound is sharp, since a rank-four matroid can fail even the basis Rayleigh inequalities.

papers.title: Skew Zero Forcing Matroids
papers.abstract: Matroid theory and skew zero forcing (SZF) in graphs are both topics of mathematical interest, but very little is known about their overlap. When a matroid arises from a graph in the traditional way, the edges of the graph correspond with the elements of the matroid. However, the SZF color change rule for graphs can be viewed as a closure operator on the vertices of a graph. As such, when a matroid arises from a graph via SZF, the vertices of the graph correspond with the elements of the matroid. We call such a matroid SZF-realizable. Notably, unlike the traditional method of obtaining a matroid from a graph, skew zero forcing in a graph does not always give rise to a matroid. This paper establishes fundamental results in graph and matroid theory with respect to (1) which matroids are SZF-realizable, and (2) what kinds of graphs do and do not give rise to SZF matroids. The main result of the paper focuses on cycle matroids of outerplanar graphs.
